title: Edited Docs Review Source Round-Trip
summary: rebuild edited Docs Review sources and import the complete reviewed source folder back to an exact scope or sub-scope
content_html:
Edited Docs Review Source Round-Trip

Result

A user can edit the persistent Markdown sources of one validated Docs Review package, rebuild its retained preview, visually accept the round trip, and import the complete edited source/ folder back to the exact canonical scope or sub-scope from which the package was prepared.

The edited Markdown folder is the content authority for this Import. The original returned JSON/JSONL package and trusted export metadata retain provenance, capability, exact membership, routing, and prepared-source version evidence; Import does not take document bodies from that original package.

This is one feature because Build alone only refreshes a preview, while source-folder Import without that refreshed preview would remove the user's explicit review step.

Workflow

returned JSON/JSONL
  -> validated Docs Review package
  -> edit package-local source/*.md
  -> Build and inspect the retained preview
  -> copy the complete source folder into Import staging
  -> preview and confirm one edited-source-folder Import
  -> overwrite the exact canonical document set

Generic Markdown Import remains body-oriented and create-only. A review source folder is a distinct trusted collection format, not a new interpretation of arbitrary standalone .md files.

Dependency Order

The feature has completed its authority and explicit Build checkpoints. Its two sub-scope Import-parity prerequisites are shipped:

  1. Sub-Scope Ordinary Document Import Delivery adds exact-collection ordinary file Import.
  2. Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery adds exact-collection returned JSON/JSONL package Import through that same report workflow.
  3. Edited Docs Review Source Round-Trip Delivery has completed ERS-1.1 and is stopped before ERS-1.2 review; it adds one shared edited-source format for both top-level scopes and configured sub-scopes, together with the Docs Review Build action.

Implementing the edited-source format before both parity deliveries would create a special sub-scope mutation path instead of extending the shared Import target, planning, confirmation, apply, and rebuild boundaries.

Stable Contract

  • The staged input is one complete source/ folder materialized by a validated Docs Review package. Individual review-source Markdown files are not accepted through ordinary Markdown Import.
  • Every direct Markdown child has strict canonical front matter and consistent review package, profile, export, scope, and optional sub-scope provenance.
  • Trusted prepared membership remains authoritative. Missing, extra, duplicate, nested, malformed, mixed-package, or cross-collection documents block the complete folder.
  • The format is overwrite-only. Every doc_id must resolve to one existing exact { scope, doc_id } or { scope, sub_scope, doc_id } target; title, filename, displayed document, and folder name never provide fallback identity.
  • Review transport fields are validated and removed. Edited body, title, and summary may apply; immutable identity, added_date, and destination-owned metadata remain canonical.
  • Preview is write-free and one confirmation covers the complete folder. Canonical source versions are revalidated immediately before an all-or- nothing source write and the appropriate scope or confined sub-scope rebuild.
  • Docs Review Build always regenerates the complete active retained preview through its existing synthetic Docs Viewer builder. Ordinary reads retain conditional repair behavior.
  • No automatic watcher, stale-file inference, selected-document Import, partial apply, or direct canonical mutation is added to Docs Review.

Import Dispatch Order

Recognition order is part of the feature contract:

  1. integrated edited-review-source recognition receives the untouched staged directory and source front matter before generic Markdown handling;
  2. one complete valid review source folder enters trusted collection preview;
  3. an individual review source is rejected with guidance to stage its complete folder; and
  4. only an unclaimed ordinary Markdown file or one-document Markdown package reaches generic front-matter stripping and create-only Import.

Generic normalization must never strip review_* provenance before the integrated recognizer can validate it, and stripped ordinary front matter must never become overwrite identity or collection routing.

Fidelity Boundary

Current document-content review source is derived Markdown. Rendering, conversion, or omitted package assets may have lost source-only or rich content. The user accepts that result by rebuilding and visually reviewing the edited package before staging its source folder.

Import reports the derived-source warning and does not reconstruct tokens, assets, comments, raw embeds, or dependencies from the original JSON/JSONL.

Full Document Export Delivery is the separate proposed owner for source-faithful outbound Markdown and asset transport. It is not a prerequisite for this feature and remains export-only unless a later delivery explicitly changes its return capability.

Feature Documents

  • Docs Import Capability Parity Quick Reference provides the compact scope/sub-scope status and delivery sequence.
  • Edited Docs Review Source Round-Trip Delivery owns the complete Build, staged-folder recognition, exact apply, and scope/sub-scope acceptance outcome.
  • Docs Review receives the shipped editable-source and explicit-Build contract at closeout.
  • Docs Import receives the shipped edited-review-source-folder format and apply contract at closeout.

Boundary

In scope:

  • one explicit Docs Review Build-to-Import workflow;
  • complete edited review-source-folder validation and confirmation;
  • overwrite-only scope and sub-scope canonical apply;
  • explicit user acceptance of current derived-Markdown fidelity; and
  • shared service and browser ownership after sub-scope Import parity.

Not in scope:

  • changing generic Markdown Import or treating arbitrary front matter as overwrite authority;
  • editing or replacing the original returned JSON/JSONL package;
  • automatic asset restoration or rich-content reconstruction;
  • making the proposed full-source export profile returnable;
  • partial folder Import, creates, deletes, moves, or identity changes; or
  • implementing either prerequisite inside this feature.
